answers.answer: 1. Start with 25 money. 2. Take 1 active association worker and 3 inactive workers. 3. Draw 8 Zoo cards, keep 4, and discard 4. 4. Draw 2 Final Scoring cards and keep them hidden. 5. Put Animals side I in the leftmost slot (strength 1); put the other four side-I Action cards randomly in the remaining slots. 6. Starting Appeal positions are 0 for the first player, 1 for the second, 2 for the third, and 3 for the fourth.

answers.answer: 1. At setup, shuffle the Base Conservation Project cards; put the top 4 face up below the Association board in a four-player game, and the top 3 in games with fewer players. 2. Only in a two-player game, cover the left level of the left face-up base project, the middle level of the middle project, and the right level of the right project; also cover the three spaces in the left donation-area column. These are blocked for both players. The summary gives no setup-blocked spaces for three or four players. 3. Reveal the six-card display after all players have chosen their opening hands.

answers.answer: 1. After using the slot-4 card, remove it, shift the cards that were left of that empty slot one space right, and put the used card in slot 1. 2. Set strength before resolving the action; each X-token spent adds +1 strength, and tokens gained during the action cannot boost that same action. 3. You may hold at most 5 X-tokens. 4. Resolve an effect that says “after finishing” only after the action is complete, including moving the Action cards.

answers.answer: 1. No: you may not take a regular action that builds zero buildings or plays zero animals; doing nothing is not legal. 2. Instead, select the alternative X-token action: take exactly 1 X-token, move that Action card to slot 1, and shift the intervening cards right; slot strength and upgrade side do not matter. 3. You cannot take this action if you already have 5 X-tokens.
answers.evidence: You may not do nothing...Use the alternative X-token action; take exactly 1 X-token...move it to slot 1...If you already have 5 X-tokens, you cannot perform this action.

answers.answer: 1. When the Break token reaches the last space, ignore any additional steps beyond the end. 2. The player who reached it gains 1 X-token. 3. Finish the current turn, then conduct the break for everyone. 4. After the break the token returns to the starting space and play continues clockwise with the next player.
answers.evidence: When it reaches the last space...break takes place after the end of your current turn, and you get 1 X-token...Ignore any additional steps...After the break, the token returns...play continues clockwise with the next player.

answers.answer: 1. Cards I first advances the Break token 2 spaces, then lets you either draw the number shown for your slot strength (maximum 3, with any required discard) or snap exactly 1 display card if strength is 5 or more. 2. Cards II also advances the Break token 2 spaces, then lets you draw from the deck and/or take cards within reputation range in any order under its upgraded table; at strength 5 it takes 4 and discards 1. 3. A Cards II snap takes exactly 1 display card at strength 3 or more, does not include a deck draw, and is not reputation-restricted; the reputation restriction applies only to the Cards II draw option. 4. Cards I and II display cards are not replenished until the end of your turn. 5. There is no in-turn hand limit; discard to the hand limit only during a break.
answers.evidence: Side I...Advance the Break token 2 spaces...draw...or snap...strength 5 or more; Side II...within reputation range...Snapping takes exactly one...reputation restriction applies only...not replenished until your turn is complete; no in-turn hand limit.

answers.answer: 1. Reputation range includes the display folder matching your Reputation counter and every lower-numbered folder. 2. Reputation 10 and above requires the upgraded Cards action. 3. Once at 15, each further reputation step gives 1 Appeal instead. 4. You may not look through the discard pile during the game.

answers.answer: 1. Build I builds exactly 1 building, of size no greater than action strength; Build II builds any number of different buildings with total size no greater than strength, but not two identical buildings in that action. 2. Buildings cost 2 money per space, paid before placement. 3. Your first building must have at least one space on a map border; later buildings must touch an existing building by at least one edge. 4. Do not build over water/rock, outside the map, over buildings, or on restricted-icon spaces until Build II. 5. Every new kiosk must be at least 3 spaces from all other kiosks. 6. Placing a pavilion immediately gives 1 Appeal, once per pavilion.

answers.answer: 1. Build I allows standard enclosures, kiosks, pavilions, and one Petting Zoo per zoo. 2. Build II additionally allows one Reptile House and one Large Bird Aviary per zoo. The game supplies four tiles of each special-enclosure type. 3. The Build action cannot build unique buildings; those enter through Sponsor cards. 4. Covering every map space except water and rock immediately gives 7 Appeal; Build II opens restricted-icon spaces, and the full-map bonus can also be triggered by other effects that cover spaces.

answers.answer: 1. Yes: bonuses gained earlier in an action, including money, cards, and newly activated workers, may be used for later steps in that action; resolve items one at a time. 2. Pay for each item before receiving that item's own benefits. For example, an animal's full cost must be payable before its play effect grants money. 3. Ordinary effects resolve immediately; effects marked “after finishing” wait until the whole action and Action-card movement are complete. 4. If effects are simultaneous, the owning player chooses their order.

answers.answer: 1. Check all left-side play conditions, then pay the Animal's printed cost; a matching-continent partner zoo reduces it by 3 money per matching continent icon on the card. 2. House it in an eligible empty standard enclosure of at least the required size, flipping that whole enclosure to occupied; some animals also require distinct adjacent water/rock spaces. Petting Zoo animals go only in the Petting Zoo; eligible reptiles and birds may instead use the Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary if their indicated capacity fits, marking occupied spaces with supply player tokens and never flipping the special enclosure. 3. Standard enclosures normally hold one animal; special enclosures can hold multiple eligible animals within their capacity. 4. Resolve ordinary play effects immediately, including before playing a second animal; resolve “after finishing” effects after the Animals action and moving its card.

At strength 5 or more, you may gain 1 Reputation at the very beginning of the action, before playing animals, so the increased range applies. 4. For each moved animal, flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all its requirements, including terrain. If none meets all requirements, flip the smallest occupied enclosure meeting its size requirement; if none meets even its size, flip none.

answers.answer: 1. Pouch tucks hand cards under the animal for 2 Appeal per card; tucked cards have no remaining function. If the animal is released, discard its tucked cards but retain the Appeal already gained. 2. Sunbathing sells up to its stated number of hand cards for 4 money each; sold cards go to the discard pile.
answers.evidence: Pouch...tuck...for two appeal per card. Tucked cards have no remaining function. If...released, discard...retain the appeal...Sunbathing...sell...four money each; sold cards go to discard.

answers.answer: 1. An extra Final Scoring card drawn before the 10-Conservation milestone joins the player's choices when they discard one card at that milestone. 2. At game end, score every remaining Final Scoring card; each card separately has a maximum of 4 Conservation points.
answers.evidence: extra Final Scoring card drawn before the 10-conservation milestone joins your choices when you discard one...At game end score every remaining...each subject to its own four-point cap.

answers.answer: 1. Shuffle the discard pile face down, draw the stated number of random cards, make the ability's stated selection, then return the discard pile face up. For Scavenging 3, draw 3 random cards, keep 1, and discard the others.
answers.evidence: shuffle the discard pile face down, draw randomly...make...selection, then return...face up. Scavenging 3 draws three...keeps one and discards the others.

answers.answer: 1. Snapping takes exactly one display card regardless of reputation; it does not draw from the deck. 2. Sponsor Magnet can take a Sponsor from the display without a reputation-range restriction; if no Sponsor is present, it has no effect. 3. Normal end-of-turn display refill applies.
answers.evidence: Snapping...exactly one display card regardless of reputation...Sponsor Magnet: display sponsors need not be in reputation range; if no sponsor...nothing happens. Ordinary end-of-turn display refill applies.

answers.answer: 1. Place Venom tokens on cards in the lowest slots first (slot 1, then 2, etc.), no more than one on a card; duplicates return to supply. 2. Using a marked card removes its token and avoids all Venom fees that turn. This includes using the X-token alternative if you have fewer than 5 X-tokens. 3. At turn end, pay 2 money only if you removed no Venom token and at least one remains on your cards; if unable, undo the turn and choose another action. You cannot avoid the fee by spending all your money. 4. Unused Venom tokens expire at the next break.
answers.evidence: lowest slots...at most one per card...Using a card with Venom removes its token...includes alternative...Pay two money at turn end only if...cannot...undo...next break clears unused tokens.

answers.answer: 1. Veterinarian gives 2/5/10 money immediately for 1/2/3 universities, respectively. 2. It reduces the strength required to support Conservation projects to 4 rather than 5. 3. Its final reward is 1 Conservation for having three universities.
answers.evidence: I: 2/5/10 money for 1/2/3 universities. R: supporting...strength 4 rather than 5. F: 1 conservation for three universities.

answers.answer: 1. Medical Breakthrough counts previously supported projects by the player tokens missing from the left edge of their zoo map, and gives 2 Appeal per such project when played. 2. At each break it gives 1 Conservation.
answers.evidence: I: 2 appeal per previously supported project (count tokens missing from the left map edge). B: 1 conservation.

answers.answer: 1. Basic Research counts each pair of different continent or animal-category icons and gives 1 Conservation per pair; Research icons do not count. 2. Each other player gains 2 money for every Conservation point you gain from it.
answers.evidence: 1 conservation per two different continent/animal-category icons; each other player gets 2 money per conservation point you gain.

answers.answer: 1. Science Library gives 1 Appeal per Research icon when played. 2. Whenever any player plays a Research icon, the Library owner gains 2 money. 3. Its final condition is five different animal categories, for 1 Conservation.
answers.evidence: I: 1 appeal per research icon. R: whenever any player plays a research icon, you...gain 2 money. F: 1 conservation with five different animal categories.

answers.answer: 1. Expert on the Americas gives 1 Appeal per Americas icon when played. 2. Each Americas icon later played into your zoo permits a free kiosk, subject to ordinary placement and kiosk-spacing rules. 3. Its final condition is five or more kiosks, for 1 Conservation.
answers.evidence: I: 1 appeal per Americas icon. R: each Americas icon played permits a free kiosk under normal placement and spacing rules. F: 1 conservation with five or more kiosks.

answers.answer: 1. Expert on Australia gives 1 Appeal per Australia icon when played. 2. Each Australia icon played lets you tuck one hand card under this Sponsor for 2 Appeal. 3. Tucked cards have no further function.
answers.evidence: I: 1 appeal per Australia icon. R: per Australia icon played...tuck one hand card...for 2 appeal; tucked cards have no further function.

answers.answer: 1. Each card places 2 supply tokens on itself; when supporting a base project below the Association board, you may return exactly one token as one icon. You may never spend both tokens on one support. 2. Only projects in the base row below the board qualify; base-origin cards later played above the board do not. 3. The final reward is 1 Conservation for five or more project supports, counted by tokens missing from the left map edge.
answers.evidence: put two supply tokens...supporting a base project below...return exactly one...never both...Base-origin cards played above...do not qualify. F: 1 conservation with five or more project supports.

answers.answer: 1. Engineer allows each Build action to add one extra copy of a building built in that same action without extra strength. 2. Pay normal money and follow placement rules; only one extra building is allowed even if several different buildings are built, and special enclosures remain limited to one of each type. 3. Its final reward is 5 Appeal for a full map except water and rock.
answers.evidence: Each Build action may add one extra copy...without additional strength. Pay normal money...only one extra...special enclosures...one-per-type...F: 5 appeal with a full map except water/rock.

answers.answer: 1. Diversity Researcher gives 2 money per water/rock icon immediately. 2. It lets you cover water/rock spaces and ignore animal and unique-building terrain requirements; the printed terrain icons still count. Terrain need not be covered to qualify for a full map. 3. Once covered, terrain no longer counts for Hydrologist, Geologist, or Architectural Zoo. 4. Its final reward is 2 Appeal per water-icon/rock-icon pair, up to three pairs.
answers.evidence: I: 2 money per water/rock icon. R: cover...ignore terrain requirements...printed terrain icons still count...Terrain need not be covered for a full map...Covered terrain stops counting...F: 2 appeal per...pair, maximum three.

answers.answer: 1. Each actual placement bonus on a border space triggers Archaeologist. 2. For each such trigger, choose any uncovered placement bonus on your map, not necessarily a border space. 3. Multiple triggers may choose the same bonus or different ones; choose their resolution order. 4. Its final condition is that all building border spaces are covered, excluding water and rock, for 1 Conservation.
answers.evidence: Every actual placement bonus on a border space grants an additional choice of any uncovered placement bonus...Several...permit several extra choices; copied bonuses can be same or different...F...all building border spaces...exclude water/rock.

answers.answer: 1. Migration Recording gives 1 X-token immediately. 2. Each Release into the Wild support gives 1 extra Conservation. You may repeatedly support the same release project with different qualifying animals, but at most once per project in one Association action. 3. Each placed token counts as a separate project support for other effects.
answers.evidence: I: 1 X-token. Each Release...support gives 1 additional conservation. You may repeatedly support...at most one token per project per Association action. Each token counts as a separate project support.

answers.answer: 1. Quarantine Lab gives 1 X-token immediately. 2. It makes you immune to Venom, Constriction, Hypnosis, and Pilfering; for Hypnosis and Pilfering, ignore your counters and choose/find the next qualifying player. 3. Its final condition is having all five continents, for 1 Conservation.
answers.evidence: I: 1 X-token. Immune to Venom, Constriction, Hypnosis and Pilfering. For latter two, ignore your counters and find next qualifying player. F: 1 conservation with all five continents.

answers.answer: 1. Permanently choose small or large, mark that choice with a supply token, and reveal deck cards until finding an animal of that type; keep it and discard the others. 2. You cannot play animals of the opposite type. 3. Chosen small animals give 2 extra Appeal, chosen large animals give 4; size-3 animals remain legal but receive no bonus.
answers.evidence: Choose small or large permanently...Reveal deck cards until finding that type...keep it...cannot play the opposite type...small...2 extra...large...4...Size-3...legal but gain no bonus.

answers.answer: 1. WAZA Small Animals Program gives 2 money per small animal when played. 2. An Animals action containing only small animals qualifies for an additional small animal from hand, with normal costs and rules; mixing small and large in the original action disqualifies it. 3. You may take one small animal from the display into hand regardless of reputation, even if you declined the extra play; ordinary display refill occurs at turn end.
answers.evidence: I: 2 money per small animal. An Animals action containing only small animals...play one additional...from hand...Mixing...prevents...may take the display animal even if declined...regardless of reputation.

answers.answer: 1. Hydrologist gives 1 Appeal per water icon when played. 2. Each newly covered space adjacent to water gives 1 money, even if spaces are in one building; a space touching multiple water hexes still pays only once. 3. Its final condition is that all water hexes are connected, with none isolated, for 1 Conservation.
answers.evidence: I: 1 appeal per water icon. R: each space newly covered adjacent to water gives 1 money...even if several...space adjacent to several...only once. F: 1 conservation if all water hexes are connected (none isolated).

answers.answer: 1. Barred Owl Hut is a unique building that must be placed when its Sponsor is played. 2. Each Bird icon played triggers drawing 2 cards from the deck, keeping one and discarding the other.
answers.evidence: 249 Barred Owl Hut: Place the unique building. R: each bird icon played draws two deck cards; keep one, discard the other.

answers.answer: 1. Place Sea Turtle Tank, its unique building, adjacent to water. 2. Each Reptile icon played lets you sell up to 2 hand cards for 4 money each; discard sold cards.
answers.evidence: Place adjacent to water. R: each reptile icon played lets you sell up to two hand cards for 4 money each; discard sold cards.

answers.answer: 1. Each Predator icon played triggers Hunter, with the number of revealed cards equal to your total Predator icons. 2. If one new card has two Predator icons, resolve two Hunters sequentially, counting both new icons when determining the second Hunter's draw count.
answers.evidence: each predator icon played uses Hunter with draws equal to your total predator icons. A double-predator card triggers two sequential Hunters, counting both new icons each time.

answers.answer: 1. Okapi Stable enters play with 3 supply tokens. For each Herbivore icon played, you may spend one token and pay money equal to a hand Sponsor's level to play that Sponsor, subject to its normal conditions. 2. Its own Herbivore icon can trigger this when the Stable is played. There are 3 uses total. 3. This effect plays a Sponsor from hand, not from display.
answers.evidence: place...three supply tokens...Per herbivore icon played...spend one token and pay money equal to a hand Sponsor’s level...normal conditions. Its own icon can trigger...Three uses total.

answers.answer: 1. Zoo School gives 1 Reputation and 1 Conservation immediately. 2. Place it so it covers at least 2 border spaces. 3. Then take one display card within reputation range or draw one card from the deck; resolve simultaneous benefits in an order you choose.
answers.evidence: I: 1 reputation, 1 conservation, place its building covering at least two border spaces, take one in-range display card or draw one deck card. Resolve simultaneous benefits in your chosen order.

answers.answer: 1. Side Entrance may cover two border spaces and, unlike ordinary buildings, need not touch an existing building; later buildings may attach to it. 2. At each break it gives 2 money per adjacent building except empty standard enclosures; it may be adjacent to a kiosk. 3. Its final reward is 5 Appeal for a full map excluding water and rock.
answers.evidence: Place on two border spaces; unlike ordinary buildings it need not touch an existing building...Later buildings may attach...B: 2 money per adjacent building except empty standard enclosures;...F: 5 appeal with a full map excluding water/rock.

answers.answer: 1. Native Farm Animals gives 1 Appeal per connected uncovered building border space; water and rock spaces never count. 2. At game end, gain 1 Conservation per six contiguous empty building spaces, evaluating each group separately and rounding down. 3. Upgrade-restricted spaces count even if Build is not upgraded; terrain spaces are excluded.
answers.evidence: I: 1 appeal per connected uncovered building border space (never water/rock). F: 1 conservation per six contiguous empty building spaces; count restricted spaces...groups...exclude water/rock.

answers.answer: 1. Explorer gives 2 money per different continent or animal-category icon immediately; Research icons do not count. 2. Each category or continent newly introduced to your zoo gives 1 Appeal and 2 money; duplicate instances of the same new icon on one card trigger that novelty reward only once.
answers.evidence: I: 2 money per different continent/animal-category icon (research does not count). R: each category/continent newly introduced...1 appeal and 2 money; a double of same new icon...only once.

answers.answer: 1. WAZA Large Animal Program immediately lets you place a free size-5 standard enclosure under ordinary placement rules. 2. When playing a large animal, it lets you ignore one left-side condition, but not terrain requirements. 3. It stacks with Research Institute, allowing two conditions to be ignored in total.
answers.evidence: I: place a size-5 standard enclosure free...R: when playing a large animal, ignore one left-side condition...Terrain requirements cannot be ignored. Stacks with Research Institute to ignore two conditions.

answers.answer: 1. Biodiverse Zoo compares your number of icons in each animal category with the player to your right; gain 1 Conservation for each category where you have more icons. 2. If that player has none in a category, one of your icons is enough to lead it. 3. The maximum is 4 Conservation.
answers.evidence: gain 1 conservation per animal category for which your zoo has more icons than the player to your right...If they have none...one icon...maximum 4.

answers.answer: 1. Observation Tower rewards only a standard enclosure adjacent to the tower hex itself, not one merely adjacent to another rock hex. 2. Special enclosures do not qualify. 3. Housing an animal there grants the two Appeal again even if an earlier animal was released. 4. The tower is not a building for kiosk income.
answers.evidence: bonus applies only to standard enclosures adjacent to tower hex itself...Special enclosures get no tower effect. Housing...gives the two appeal again...tower is not a building for kiosk income.

answers.answer: 1. Outdoor Areas applies to a standard enclosure touching its Outdoor Area hex, not merely another water hex. 2. It counts as two spaces larger for all purposes after placement; a size-2 enclosure there is treated as size 4. 3. You cannot ignore this when releasing or transferring animals. 4. It does not affect special enclosures and is not a building.
answers.evidence: standard enclosure touching the Outdoor Area hex...counts as two spaces larger for all purposes after placement...cannot be ignored on release or transfer...No effect on special enclosures...not a building.

answers.answer: 1. A building on Commercial Harbor's adjacent building space activates it; your first building may start beside the Harbor but need not. 2. Its discard ability may be used once per your own turn, before, during, or after your action, never during breaks or another player's turn. 3. The Harbor is not a building.
answers.evidence: a building on its adjacent building space connects/activates it. Your first building may begin there but need not...discard ability...before, during or after...only once per own turn...Harbor is not a building.

answers.answer: 1. Park Restaurant break income is 1 money per adjacent covered hex, not per building; empty enclosures qualify, and multiple hexes of one building each count. 2. The Restaurant is not a building for kiosk income. 3. Its special-enclosure placement bonus gives one free Reptile House or one free Large Bird Aviary, even before Build II; choose only one and obey other normal placement rules.
answers.evidence: break income is one money per adjacent covered hex, regardless of building type, occupancy or several hexes...Restaurant is not a building...bonus gives one Reptile House or one Large Bird Aviary free...Choose one, not both.

answers.answer: 1. Cover Hollywood Hills H spaces with buildings using ordinary placement rules; each time an H is covered, reveal deck cards until a Sponsor appears, keep it, and discard the others. 2. H spaces are not placement bonuses and do not trigger Archaeologist. 3. After all three H spaces are covered, every Sponsor's level is one lower. 4. Upgrade restrictions remain: third/fourth partner zoos require Association II, and upgrade-marked spaces require Build II even for bonus buildings.
answers.evidence: cover H spaces...ordinary placement...reveal...Sponsor...H is not a placement bonus...After covering all three...Sponsor's level...bonus partner zoos still require Association II...Build II...

answers.answer: 1. Pay money equal to the Sponsor's level and meet its usual play conditions. 2. Play the Sponsor from hand only, even with Sponsors II; it cannot come from the display for this bonus. 3. The Sponsors Action card stays in its current slot and does not move.
answers.evidence: paid-Sponsor effect costs money equal to...level and requires usual conditions. Play it only from hand, even if Sponsors is upgraded...leaves Sponsors Action card in its current slot.

answers.answer: 1. Appeal cannot exceed 113, and Conservation cannot exceed 41; any gains past those track ends are lost.
answers.evidence: Appeal cannot exceed 113, nor conservation 41; gains beyond those ends are lost.

answers.answer: 1. Venom affects every other zoo with higher Appeal than yours; each such zoo must have at least 5 Appeal. 2. Hypnosis selects among tied highest-Appeal zoos meeting the 5-Appeal floor, has no effect if you are selected, and copies only slot 1, 2, or 3. 3. Pilfering 1 selects a highest-Appeal qualifying zoo; Pilfering 2 resolves the highest-Appeal and most-Conservation qualifying targets separately, with the latter requiring at least 1 Conservation; ties are selectable and a self-target has no effect. 4. Constriction affects every other qualifying zoo ahead on Appeal and/or Conservation: one track gives 1 token, both gives 2, placed in slots 5 and 4 respectively.
answers.evidence: Interactive target reference: every affected zoo...5 appeal; Venom...higher appeal; Hypnosis...highest...slot 1,2,3; Pilfering...highest...most conservation...; Constriction...ahead...one token...two tokens...slots 4 and 5.

answers.answer: 1. An Animal card's partner-zoo condition requires a partner zoo from its specified continent; a Sponsor card's partner-zoo condition can be met by a partner zoo from any continent. 2. A maximum-25-Appeal condition permits play only while your Appeal is at most 25; its marker is only a reminder, not a general track cap. 3. A minimum-Reputation condition requires at least the printed reputation. 4. An ignore-one-condition bonus removes one left-edge condition, but cannot remove a terrain requirement.
answers.evidence: Animal partner-zoo condition means a partner from its continent; Sponsor...any continent. A left-side maximum 25...at most 25...minimum-reputation...at least...ignore-one-condition...does not remove terrain requirements.

answers.answer: 1. Crested Porcupine's Digging 2 lets you choose up to twice between discarding a display card and replacing it, or discarding a hand card and drawing one card from the deck. 2. You may choose a different option for the second selection.
answers.evidence: choose up to twice between discarding a display card and replenishing it, or discarding a hand card then drawing one deck card. Decide again after each card which option to use.

answers.answer: 1. After taking display cards, move cards from higher-numbered folders down while preserving their order, then fill empty spaces from the deck. 2. During Digging, replacing a discarded display card happens immediately by shifting higher folders down and drawing into folder 6.
answers.evidence: move cards from higher-numbered folders down (keeping their order), then fill empty spaces from the deck; Digging...replaced immediately, shifting higher folders down and drawing into folder 6.

answers.answer: 1. Build standard enclosures empty side up, showing the yellow border and size number. 2. Each placement-bonus space covered gives its bonus immediately, once; turning the enclosure occupied later does not grant the covered bonus again.
answers.evidence: Place...standard enclosure empty side up (yellow border and size number). Each placement-bonus icon covered is awarded immediately once...does not award...again.

answers.answer: 1. When the first player reaches 10 Conservation, each player discards one Final Scoring card face down under the remaining Final Scoring pile.
answers.evidence: all players choose and discard one of their Final Scoring cards (face down under the remaining pile).

answers.answer: 1. Randomly determine the starting player; turn order proceeds clockwise, one player at a time, without formal rounds. 2. On each turn you perform one action using an Action card. Additional effects or bonuses may grant further action resolution as specified by the effect, but the ordinary turn begins with one chosen Action card and its action.
answers.evidence: Randomly determine a start player. Turn order is clockwise. Ark Nova does not play in formal rounds...On your turn you always perform one action...

answers.answer: 1. If no player reaches 10 Conservation before the game ends, all players must discard one Final Scoring card before end-game scoring begins.
answers.evidence: If no one reaches 10 conservation points before the game ends, all players must discard one Final Scoring card before end-game scoring begins.
